outcome: Neonatal short-term outcomes (APGAR scores, umbilical cord pH, asphyxia, NICU admission, NICU length of stay)
cohort: The study participants were women with singleton breech pregnancies at >36+0 weeks of gestation.
finding: Vaginal breech delivery is associated with lower APGAR scores and umbilical arterial pH compared to caesarean section, and MRI pelvimetry may improve newborn outcomes by aiding selection.
mod_finding: Planned vaginal breech delivery was associated with lower APGAR scores and umbilical arterial pH compared to planned caesarean section, but no significant difference in asphyxia or NICU admission rate, although infants admitted to NICU after vaginal delivery had shorter stays.
followup_time: Short-term (immediate postnatal period, including NICU stay length)
birth_weight: N/A (birth weight was a covariate in analysis)
